# owner: platform
"""Plain text absence notices for parents."""

import rosterkit.models
import rosterkit.errors
import rosterkit.attendance


# ---
def absence_notice(student, marks):
    """Short notice naming the student, days missed and the dates in order."""
    mark_list = list(marks)
    # every mark has to belong to the student the notice is about
    for mark in mark_list:
        if mark.student_id != student.student_id:
            raise rosterkit.errors.ProjectError(
                f"mark for student {mark.student_id!r} does not belong to {student.student_id!r}"
            )

    missed = rosterkit.attendance.days_missed(mark_list)
    if not missed:
        raise rosterkit.errors.ProjectError(
            f"no absences to report for student {student.student_id!r}"
        )

    dates = []
    # dates come back oldest first, so the notice keeps that order
    for when in missed:
        dates.append(when.isoformat())

    name = f"{student.first_name} {student.last_name}"
    count = len(missed)
    unit = "day" if count == 1 else "days"
    return (
        f"Dear parent or guardian of {name},\n"
        f"{name} missed {count} {unit} of class.\n"
        f"Dates absent: {', '.join(dates)}"
    )
EOF
cat > tests/test_notices.py <<'EOF'
# owner: platform
import unittest

import rosterkit.notices
import rosterkit.models
import rosterkit.errors
import datetime


STUDENT = rosterkit.models.Student("7", "Rivera", "Ana", "A")


def make_mark(student_id, month, status):
    return rosterkit.models.Mark(student_id, datetime.date(2026, month, 3), status)


class AbsenceNoticeTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_notice_names_student_count_and_ordered_dates(self):
        """The notice lists absent dates oldest first."""
        marks = [
            make_mark("7", 5, "absent"),
            make_mark("7", 4, "present"),
            make_mark("7", 2, "absent"),
        ]
        text = rosterkit.notices.absence_notice(STUDENT, marks)
        self.assertTrue("Ana Rivera" in text)
        self.assertTrue("2 days" in text)
        self.assertTrue("2026-02-03, 2026-05-03" in text)

    def test_single_absence_uses_singular(self):
        """One missed day reads as 1 day."""
        text = rosterkit.notices.absence_notice(STUDENT, [make_mark("7", 2, "absent")])
        self.assertTrue("1 day " in text)

    def test_excused_days_are_left_out(self):
        """Excused days are not reported as absences."""
        marks = [make_mark("7", 2, "absent"), make_mark("7", 3, "excused")]
        text = rosterkit.notices.absence_notice(STUDENT, marks)
        self.assertFalse("2026-03-03" in text)

    def test_foreign_mark_is_rejected(self):
        """A mark for another student raises ProjectError."""
        marks = [make_mark("7", 2, "absent"), make_mark("8", 2, "absent")]
        with self.assertRaises(rosterkit.errors.ProjectError):
            rosterkit.notices.absence_notice(STUDENT, marks)

    def test_no_absences_is_rejected(self):
        """Having nothing to report raises ProjectError."""
        with self.assertRaises(rosterkit.errors.ProjectError):
            rosterkit.notices.absence_notice(STUDENT, [make_mark("7", 2, "present")])
EOF

trace.final_message:
I added `absence_notice(student, marks)` in `rosterkit/notices.py`. It builds a short notice with the student's name, the number of days missed and the absent dates oldest first, and it raises `ProjectError` if any mark belongs to another student or there are no absences. Excused days don't count as absences. I also added five tests in `tests/test_notices.py`, a line each in `CHANGES.txt` and `docs/api.txt`, and committed it all as 084802a; `make check` passes with 31 tests and the lint script reports no syntax errors.

The new code follows the repo's CLAUDE.md style rules, which differ from some older modules, for example plain `import module` instead of `from ... import`.
